info.title: SCI Healthcare API
info.description: Read-only API for the SCI Healthcare care-voucher protocol on Stellar. All monetary amounts are decimal strings representing i128 values in base units (stroops). A 7-decimal Stellar asset like USDC uses 10^7 base units per whole token, so "30000000" = 3.0000000 USDC. Amounts are strings, not numbers, because they can exceed Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER.

ErrorEnvelope.description: The single error body every route answers with, whatever layer refused the request: a thrown `ApiError`, a rate-limit rejection, a database outage or a crash all reach the client in this shape. `error` is the stable, never-localised code to switch on; `message` is written for a human and follows `Accept-Language`; `details` appears when the refusal names the failing parameter.

error.description: Machine-readable code, e.g. `invalid_query`, `voucher_not_found`, `rate_limited`, `database_unavailable`. Clients switch on this, not on `message`.

message.description: Human-readable description, localised from the request `Accept-Language`. Subject to change; never a matching key.

details.description: Validation issues for the offending parameters when the route has them. Shape and key (`details`, or `issues` on two routes) follow the library that produced them.

get.summary: List clinics, optionally filtered by service and sortable
get.description: Filters: `status`, `country`, `q` (name contains, case-insensitive) and `serviceCode` (clinics with that service active). Sorts by `sort=name`, `registered` (default) or `country`, with `order=asc` or `desc` (default: `desc` for `registered`, `asc` otherwise). The sort and order are encoded in `nextCursor`; a cursor from another ordering is `400 invalid_cursor`.

200.description: A page of clinics with their active services. Filter by `status`, `country`, `q` or `serviceCode` (only clinics with that service active); sort by `name`, `registered` (default, newest first) or `country`, with `order=asc|desc`. `nextCursor` encodes the ordering and answers `400 invalid_cursor` if used with another one; `total` is only present without a cursor, because a keyset page does not count. `capacity` is the clinic voucher cap the indexer read from the registry, `null` until the clinic has ever set one (`0` means unlimited), and `openVouchers` counts its `Funded` and `Claimed` vouchers.

get.summary: A clinic's services and price list
get.description: Filters: `active=true` or `active=false` to take only the listed or only the delisted half of the catalogue (both by default), `sort=price` (default) or `sort=code`, and `order=asc` (default) or `desc`. Equal prices always order by code ascending.

get.summary: Live voucher updates (server-sent events)
get.description: Streams voucher state transitions as the indexer commits them. Requires exactly one of `voucher` or `provider`. Each frame carries the on-chain event id in an `id:` line; send it back as the `Last-Event-ID` header on reconnect to replay up to 500 later events in order before going live. If that cursor is too old to replay, the server sends one `event: reset` frame with `{"type":"reset","reason":...}` and the client must refetch. Each `data:` frame is one JSON object with `id`, `type`, `voucherId`, `providerAddress`, `status`, `ledger`, `txHash` and `at`; it never contains a beneficiary reference. Comment lines are heartbeats.

200.description: A server-sent event stream: one frame per committed voucher state change matching the filter, comment lines as heartbeats. A frame carries the on-chain event id in an `id:` line and a JSON object with `id`, `type`, `voucherId`, `providerAddress`, `status`, `ledger`, `txHash` and `at` — the same facts the JSON routes expose for that transition, and never a beneficiary reference. Send the last `id:` back as `Last-Event-ID` to replay up to 500 later events in order before going live; if the cursor is too old, one `event: reset` frame says to refetch. The example shows a first connect, one frame and a heartbeat.
